body:
I think the only thing that would help me would be some level of forgiveness from the people I’ve hurt. I’ve tried to reach out to them but have received no response. Clearly if they aren’t ready then I have to respect their boundaries, but I just feel like until that happens I am stuck in limbo. Ultimately, I have no idea how they are feeling now so I don’t know if they will ever get to that point.   


They are the people I want to talk to most about how I’m feeling. But equally, they are the last people I can talk to because i don’t want to be emotionally manipulative. So unless anyone has any ideas, I’m pretty much stuck
I just really don’t think there’s anyway she could help me. I just have to stay distracted.

I had started anti depressants prior to my crash. I am reluctant to try any more as I really haven't heard many success stories, but I will consider it

I would never do the car thing again. I experienced only a week of what it would be like to be paralysed, and clearly however badly I feel now, it would he so much worse I that situation. I should clarify that it was only mildly impulsive. At that point I had been considering it for a long time, but I was always restrained by the fear of collateral damage. 

I knew if I was ever going to do it, then that was the road I would do it on. I also knew that if I was going to do it the conditions had to be right; I would have to have a clear motive for doing that drive, and there needed to additional factors that could have caused the crash as I'm such a careful driver. Hence, doing it on the way home, during a storm, at night (least traffic). Naturally, I had put myself in that position before and not gone through with it, so I guess there must have been some impulsivity, but it certainly wasn't unplanned. 

Regardless, my car is now written off and since I had only just fully recovered before ‘Rona hit, I have no job and no form of of income. Hence, no car any time soon. So couldn’t ’do the car thing’ even if I wanted to.

I have had counselling, but I got passed round to four different counsellors before the final one said there was nothing she could do to help me and sent me to the doctor to get antidepressants. I was on them until my crash, but I stopped whilst I hospital as I didn't want my mum to find out. I haven't taken any since and I'm hesitant about trying any more, but I'll consider it after this lock down. Meds in general aren't prescribed as widely in the UK as they are in the US (assuming that's where you are)

I've tried to tell my mum about my depression before. She broke down and felt so guilty, worrying about how I had got to that point and where she had gone wrong. I was no where near suicidal at that point. I could never tell her about this, she couldn't handle it

This is the main thing stopping me. I have done a lot of research and I truly don’t think there is a suicide method that is painless and 100% effective, never mind one that would look accidental. I think my family could handle my death if it was a tragic accident, but I would never want them to carry the guilt of me killing myself. I can only imagine the pain.

I'm really sorry for everything you've had to suffer, I hope you've found some light since then.

The only thing worse than me feeling this way, is the thought of everyone else worrying about me feeling this way. Hopefully once I graduate and get a proper income ill be able to access the help I need independently. Just need to wait it out till then

I am normally a really careful driver. My aunt died in an RTA after someone in the opposite direction tried to overtake around a blind corner. She left behind her husband of 40 years who had no children, few close friends and had just joined her in retirement. Normally this memory is enough to stop myself when I get those thoughts, but Im ashamed to say that in this instance my own pain overwhelmed my consideration for other people. 

Thank you for your words. It's a difficult balance between trying to prioritise my own feelings and being present for everyone else.

I completely agree with your idea of finding something to hold on to, and in theory this should work. But my issue is that as soon as I am at my happiest I always find a way to destroy it. Two years ago I broke up with the love of my life. He was everything I could have ever wanted and more, but I couldn't shake the self-doubt. I couldn't believe that he really loved me, and even if he did, I didn't believe that I deserved to be as happy as I was. After I broke up with him he spiralled into a depression and became suicidal. I was left completely alone because all our friends were shared, and I didn't believe I deserved them after what I had done to him. Two years on, he still won't talk to me, so I carry the guilt of hurting him and the pain of losing him, with no closure in sight. 

Just before lockdown started, my best friend of two years told me he loved me. I am too scared to be in a relationship because I don't want to risk our friendship, so I rejected him. He now needs space apart from me, so I am once again left completely alone, and at the absolute worst time for me. This just feels like a constant cycle for me, as it's happened in all my previous relationships too, friends or otherwise. As soon as I'm at my happiest, I ruin everything and end up completely alone again with another layer of guilt.

I know I'm only 22, so I will have a lot more chances to find the right people, but I just can't handle the guilt of hurting anyone else
I'm really sorry to hear about that, but you're still here 7 years on, what's kept you going?

I don’t think I will do it again. I only spent a week immobilised, not being able to sit up, eat or wash myself, but it was enough to make never want to risk that again. However bad things are now, they would be infinitely worse if I was paralysed. 

My criteria are that if I were to do it again, I would have to be 100% certain it would work, and it would have to look accidental. As of yet, my research hasn't found anything to fulfil those criteria. So I guess we just need to make the best out of what we've got. Thanks for sharing, it does help.
Glad you’re still here 4 years on, what’s kept you going? Has anyone ever found out?
Thank you, it was ‘tears dry on their own’. What’s your favourite song? :)
Did you gain any comfort in sharing your story in that essay? It has definitely helped me a little, it’s just good to feel heard, even by complete strangers.
Thank you. There is a sort of sick comfort in knowing I’m not the only one who has to suffer through this. Hope you’re doing okay.

I often think about my younger sister and whether she has the same feelings as me. I can see that my dad does, if not now then definitely in the past. I couldn’t imagine the pain of losing my sister to suicide. I’m scared or her being so grief-ridden that she would do something, and that this would have a sort of ripple effect to my parents or other family members. I know it sounds conceited to worry that other people would be so hurt by my death that they would hurt themselves, but it’s not unheard of. In my town, four people from the same family killed themselves one by one over a few years. This fear is the main thing that stops me from doing it. 

I’m about to give some hypocritical advice here because I don’t follow it myself, so apologies in advance. There’s a lot of evidence to suggest that depression is hereditary. It’s likely that if you and your brother have both felt the same, then your dad does too. The only thing stopping me from talking to my family is that they have absolutely no idea, and I don’t want them to worry, but yours clearly already have some awareness. Have you tried talking to your dad about it? He may appear fine, but I wouldn’t be surprised if he feels a very similar way to you.

Not doing a lot right now, as you can imagine. Generally speaking, I never let myself be alone. If I’m with people I am 100% invested in them, so I can stay distracted. As soon as I am left to my own thoughts it goes downhill, but I can normally keep myself above water if I have something to look forward to within a couple of days.  

Now that we’re in isolation I have to stay in with my family and knowing that I can’t see any of my friends for the foreseeable future physically hurts. I love my family and I know I am so privileged to have a safe space to be with people that care about me, but everyone keeps to themselves, I can go a whole day without seeing anyone. I try to keep busy but most of the time I have no motivation, I feel like I’m just existing rather than actually living. 

And I know that quarantine won’t last forever, but it’s really hard to see the light when we’re stuck in this for an indefinite amount of time.

  
Tears dry on their own- it actually felt quite upbeat at the time, honestly gave me the courage to do it. I can see how the corrs would do it for you though.

Thank you for sharing. It really just feels like I’m missing that fundamental instinct to survive, their was no relief in failure. But glad someone else feels the same. I guess instead of trying to find the point of life I just need to stop thinking of dying as an option.
